definition: the phone call at twenty that seeded twenty years of daily practice

settled:
It started in an emergency, on a phone line, when I was about twenty. My nervous system was already broken, my body shook by default, I could not leave the flat, and going home was not something I could let myself consider.

I got a church psychologist in Germany on the phone. His stress assessment put me at the ninety-ninth percentile. I could not have scored higher.

He taught me the main systems of the body and how they tie into the autonomic nervous system, and that breathing is the one semi-voluntary bridge into it. I cannot will my heart rate or my sympathetic tone. I can steer them through the breath.

That one idea is the whole foundation. Four in and twelve out is the engineered form of a longer exhale tipping the balance toward parasympathetic.

From one call, when I could not leave the room, to hours of every day, twenty years on.
